clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old female presented with sudden retrosternal chest pain radiating to neck, with dysphagia, throat pain, voice changes, and positional shortness of breath, without trauma or precipitating events. Initial chest X-ray revealed mediastinal air. Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed retropharyngeal air extending to the mediastinum and anterior chest surgical emphysema without foreign body. Contrast esophagography with Gastrografin and Barium was negative for leakage. Esophagoscopy revealed no mucosal injury or foreign body. The patient stabilized clinically the next day with symptom resolution. Follow-up imaging one week post-discharge demonstrated complete resolution of retropharyngeal air and mediastinal emphysema. The diagnosis of spontaneous esophageal rupture was made despite negative direct visualization and contrast studies, supported clinically and radiographically by mediastinal emphysema and symptomatology, with no precipitating factors identified.
